title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'small-sample-size' across 4 independent papers
explanation: 4 independent papers (1988–2017) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'small-sample-size'. Mixed-fidelity: 2 full-text, 2 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.743 vs uncorrected 0.657. Methodological diversity: 4 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. CAVEAT: 'small-sample-size' is a generic methodological category; it may fail the actionability 'named object of study' bar. Example limitation statements: The study intervention was evaluated on a small sample size of 13 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus over  | The number of documented cases of subarachnoid hemorrhage was small (28 cases). | Small sample sizes in specific sub-analyses, such as the 11 longitudinal participants who initiated metformin,. Papers: openalex:W2127264189; openalex:W2315875886; openalex:W2323151514; openalex:W2589088833.

caveats.label: Mixed-fidelity
caveats.detail: 2 supporting paper(s) are abstract-only, which yield ~11x fewer own-work limitations than full text.

caveats.label: Generic category
caveats.detail: The limitation category is generic and may fail the actionability bar.

consumer.headline: 4 separate teams ran into the same wall: tested on too few examples
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 4 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 2 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Based partly on summaries only
caveats.text: For some of these papers we only had the summary, not the full text. Papers we could read in full reveal far more about their own limits, so this may be built on an incomplete picture.

caveats.label: Broadly worded
caveats.text: The problem these papers describe is worded broadly enough that they may not be running into quite the same thing.
